facts.statement: A numerical dtype specifies a representable value range and a bit width, so candidate integer and floating types need not preserve the same input values.
Inspect a.dtype and explicitly cast with a.astype(candidate_dtype) when comparing representations.
For a fixed-width numerical array, a.size × a.itemsize is its element-storage byte count, exposed by a.nbytes; it excludes non-element object overhead.
Compare the cast values with the reference values using arithmetic differences before accepting a lower-precision representation; casting can overflow or lose precision.

practice.objective: Write the NumPy import and a learner-defined Python function that compares two supplied numerical dtypes for the six-value order feature matrix. Retain the reference matrix, explicitly cast it into each candidate dtype, inspect each dtype, calculate element-storage bytes, and use scalar arithmetic differences to check every value against the supplied tolerance and range requirements. Return the choice and its justification under the declared storage budget, or report that neither candidate satisfies the requirements.
practice.success: Both candidates are explicitly cast from the unchanged reference. Their element counts remain unchanged, their size-times-itemsize totals agree with nbytes, and every supplied value—including boundary fixtures—is checked against the reference. The returned justification distinguishes element storage from total object memory and accepts only a candidate satisfying the declared value-preservation and storage requirements.

live_code.required_skill: Implement a bounded dtype comparison using explicit casts, element-storage accounting, and scalar arithmetic checks.
blocked_syntax: sklearn preprocessing, fit, and predict calls
torch tensor construction and training calls
cloud storage or managed-training client calls
live_code.starter_state_intent: The supplied infrastructure provides the six-value order feature matrix a, two candidate dtype specifications, reference-value and boundary fixtures, a numeric tolerance, and an element-storage budget. It supplies no completed comparison function or imports. The learner works only with this in-memory fixture and leaves its reference values unchanged.
live_code.observable_success: The returned result records each candidate dtype, unchanged element count, calculated bytes, nbytes, scalar differences for all six reference values, and acceptance status. The final choice is supported by both preservation checks and the declared budget, with an explicit explanation if neither candidate qualifies.
